title: Liminal, the game engine for agents. (Open Source)
author: succulent999
selftext:
I've always loved game development, and with the innovation of agentic development, what better idea than to give Claude its own game development environment!

My friend and I created a game engine for agents, "Liminal". Completely free and open-source, Liminal has MCP integration, Skills for development, one-click static platform builds, a Unity-like scene editor with Cameras, an element inspector, Lua scripting, and more.

This idea spun off when I was attempting to create a PSX-style retro 3D game using Claude's Fable 5.

It's usable agentically AND traditionally via the Liminal editor app. It comes with themes, customizable window layouts (ImGUI), and built-in playtesting.

The built-in Lua library also has local LLM inference capabilities via llama.cpp, this can be used to integrate LLM technology into your game during gameplay! (Need a capable computer or use a crappy model!)

Give it a try, let us know what you think, and maybe even throw in a PR with new features. This is a big passion project for me, and I want to make it the best it can be.

(A pre-built binary is available for MacOS. Windows and Linux can be built from source)

Here is the GitHub page: [https://github.com/Wilcus-Industries/liminal](https://github.com/Wilcus-Industries/liminal)

Here is the Website (WIP): [https://liminal.wilcus.com](https://liminal.wilcus.com/)

comments.author: TopTippityTop
comments.body: How does it compare with Godot?

replies.author: succulent999
replies.body: I’ve only been working on this for a few weeks now carefully testing, I wouldn’t dare compare my work to Godot just yet lol

replies.author: Jlocke98
replies.body: Perhaps a better question is what is better about your engine that justified the rewrite instead of extending godot?

replies.author: succulent999
replies.body:
The idea behind Liminal, which (I think) justifies yet another game engine, is that it is "a game engine" specifically for an agent to interface with. Years ago, I experimented with creating my own game engine, and really, there was no reason other than learning. Now, with the exponential growth of agentic engineering and development, giving agents MCPs, tools, and skills is becoming super popular.

Now, when I hear people "creating Minecraft in one prompt" using models like Fable 5, sure they may have a running game written using a big framework like Three.js, or maybe even OpenGL, this requires the agent to create its own baseline for the game to run on, including the engine, the ECS system, etc., what Liminal does is provide these baseline features, requiring the agent to simply create scenes, organize your assets into place, and write simple component scripts.

In short, I think a stupid-simple way to think about it is that creating a game in Unity is simply easier/faster than it would be creating a game from scratch in OpenGL, putting this in the agents perspective, creating a full game in OpenGL would use up more context, more tokens, where giving your agent Liminal it would have all of the bells and whistles for itself.

Another added benefit is that you can open up the project the agent is working on inside the editor itself and have a look at exactly how everything is arranged visibly, whereas you would need to learn a whole codebase if the agent wrote the game using OpenGL.

Sorry, I know that was quite long. This has been a very passionate project for me.

replies.author: Jlocke98
replies.body: I appreciate the long form explanation. It sounds like the act of one shotting games would be a good benchmark and way to promote your engine.
